visual: Small, upright, bushy hardy fuchsia with bronze-green foliage tinged purple and abundant small semi-double flowers combining rose-pink outer parts with white, pink-veined petals.
water: Keep reasonably moist during active growth, particularly while flowering and when grown in containers, but allow excess water to drain freely.
aspect: Full sun to partial shade in a sheltered position protected from cold, drying winds.
soil: Fertile, moist but well-drained soil; tolerant of acid, neutral and alkaline conditions and a wide range of soil textures.
soilWarning: Avoid prolonged waterlogging and extremely exposed, drying sites, particularly during winter.
prune: Prune in spring once new growth begins, removing dead or frost-damaged stems and cutting established shoots back to strong healthy buds as required.
cvs: Alice Hoffman; compact semi-double hardy fuchsia cultivar.
hardinessNote: Hardy through most of the UK to roughly -10 to -5°C when established. Plant slightly deeper, mulch the root area in winter and provide shelter in colder gardens.
resilience: Reliable hardy fuchsia capable of returning from the base after winter damage, though severe frost and exposed container culture increase risk.
uses: Flower borders, cottage gardens, courtyard planting, edging and patio containers.
foliage: Deciduous bronze-green leaves with purple tinges on a compact bushy framework.
container: Good, although container-grown roots require more winter protection than plants established in the ground.
uncertain: Some commercial listings give heights up to around 90 cm, while RHS describes 'Alice Hoffman' as a small shrub around 60 cm tall; 50–60 cm is used here for its usual compact garden habit.

visual: Dense, compact, broadly rounded deciduous shrub with thorny branching and unusually vivid colour-changing foliage. Small pale yellow flowers tinged red are followed by bright red berries.
water: Water regularly during establishment. Once established, water mainly during prolonged dry periods or when grown in containers.
aspect: Full sun to partial shade; strongest foliage colour, flowering and fruiting occur in good sun.
soil: Adaptable to most garden soils provided drainage is reasonable.
prune: Little pruning is required. Remove misplaced, damaged or congested shoots and trim hedging after flowering if necessary.
toxicity: Berries are ornamental and should not be eaten. Stems are thorny, so wear gloves when handling or pruning.
cvs: Neon Series; compact Polish cultivar introduced commercially in 2021.
hardinessNote: Extremely hardy and suitable for even very cold UK gardens.
resilience: Very cold hardy, adaptable to a wide range of soils and relatively tolerant once established.
uses: Shrub borders, colourful foliage schemes, low hedging, urban planting, wildlife gardens and containers.
foliage: Deciduous oval leaves with striking seasonal colour changes from orange and red to green and finally orange-red.
container: Good; compact habit makes it suitable for substantial outdoor containers.
uncertain: Published size information varies. Current RHS information places it within roughly 0.5–1 m, while breeder and nursery descriptions commonly describe a compact plant around 60–80 cm.

visual: Compact, rounded and densely branched perennial producing masses of small white daisy-like flowers with bright yellow centres above fresh green foliage.
water: Water regularly while establishing and during prolonged dry weather. Keep container plants evenly moist during flowering.
aspect: Full sun to partial shade, with strongest flowering generally in good light.
soil: Moderately fertile, moist but well-drained soil.
soilWarning: Avoid persistently waterlogged winter soil. Good airflow helps reduce mildew problems.
prune: Deadhead to keep plants tidy if required, then cut old stems down to near ground level after flowering or in late winter.
cvs: Alpha White; compact white-flowered selection commonly sold within the Alpha range.
hardinessNote: Fully hardy through UK winters in well-drained soil, dying back before returning from the crown in spring.
resilience: Reliable hardy perennial with strong late-season flowering and good cold tolerance.
uses: Front of borders, cottage gardens, containers, mixed perennial displays and late-season pollinator planting.
foliage: Dense fresh to dark green herbaceous foliage, dying back during winter.
container: Very good due to its naturally compact, mound-forming habit.
uncertain: UK retailers commonly list this plant as Aster dumosus 'Alpha White'. Modern taxonomy places Aster dumosus within Symphyotrichum, hence Symphyotrichum dumosum 'Alpha White' is used here.

visual: Compact, mound-forming bedding pansy carrying broad, overlapping rose-pink flowers marked by a dark face or blotch around the flower centre.
water: Keep evenly moist but not saturated, watering more frequently in containers and during dry flowering periods.
aspect: Full sun to partial shade. Best flowering occurs in bright conditions during cool weather.
soil: Fertile, humus-rich, moist but well-drained soil.
soilWarning: Avoid waterlogged compost and excessively hot, dry positions; pansies generally perform poorly during sustained summer heat.
prune: Deadhead regularly to prolong flowering and trim back tired or leggy growth when necessary.
cvs: Rose Blotch colour selection; commercial Matrix Rose Blotch also exists, but the supplied label does not identify the series.
hardinessNote: Very cold tolerant as a bedding pansy, although prolonged severe weather, saturated soil and exposed containers can still cause losses.
resilience: Excellent cool-season bedding performance and tolerant of frost; less resilient in sustained summer heat.
uses: Bedding, borders, edging, window boxes, patio containers, baskets and seasonal displays.
foliage: Compact green to dark green, scalloped foliage forming a low mound; usually semi-evergreen in mild conditions.
container: Excellent for pots, troughs, window boxes and mixed seasonal containers.
uncertain: Several commercial pansy ranges use a Rose Blotch colour. Matrix Rose Blotch is a documented cultivar selection, but the supplied nursery wording does not confirm that this plant belongs to the Matrix Series.

aspect: Full sun in a warm, sheltered position.
soilWarning: Avoid persistently wet, cold or poorly drained soil.
prune: No formal pruning required. Deadhead or regularly cut flower stems to encourage continued flowering.
cvs: Species supplied without a named cultivar.
hardinessNote: Tender to frost in the UK and normally grown as a half-hardy annual.
resilience: Very tolerant of summer heat and increasingly drought tolerant once established, but killed by frost.

latin: Cyclamen persicum Super Serie Djix F1
visual: Compact mini cyclamen with heart-shaped, silver-marbled leaves and distinctive flowers whose petals point downwards rather than strongly reflexing upwards, giving Djix its unusual umbrella-like flower shape.
water: Water moderately while actively growing, preferably from below or around the edge of the pot. Allow excess water to drain and reduce watering markedly as the plant enters dormancy.
aspect: Bright filtered light or partial shade in a cool, sheltered position. Avoid hot, dry indoor air and intense midday sun behind glass.
soil: Free-draining, peat-free loam-based potting compost with good aeration.
soilWarning: Do not leave the tuber or crown sitting wet. Waterlogging encourages root and crown rots.
prune: No pruning required. Remove spent flowers and yellowing leaves cleanly from the base.
toxicity: Tuber is harmful if eaten; wear gloves if handling causes skin irritation.
cvs: Super Serie Djix F1; Schoneveld mini Cyclamen persicum selection bred for unusual downward-facing flowers, heat tolerance and long shelf life.
hardinessNote: Tender in the UK and not frost hardy. Best protected indoors, under glass or in very sheltered seasonal containers.
resilience: Unusually heat tolerant for a mini cyclamen and bred for continued bud production and good shelf life, but still vulnerable to frost and prolonged wet compost.
uses: Indoor pots, cool conservatories, porches and sheltered autumn container displays.
foliage: herbaceous; dark green, heart-shaped leaves with decorative silver marbling; tuberous perennial with seasonal dormancy.
container: Excellent; specifically bred as a compact pot cyclamen.
uncertain: The supplied label says 'Djix Pink', but Schoneveld's current Super Serie Djix range lists Red, Wine Red and Salmon with Eye rather than a formal Pink colour. The exact colour selection should therefore be confirmed from the plant or original grower label.
P7 appears to refer to approximately a 7 cm nursery pot rather than part of the cultivar name.
